description: Review a Code session's branch diff. Store your review of a Code session's changes: the branch against its base, as the Diff view's Branch comparison shows it, which is what a pull request shows. The user reads each comment inline under its lines and dismisses the ones they disagree with; Send delivers the rest to the session's agent with their own comments. A review replaces your earlier one for the session, so send the whole review each time. Every comment names a file in that diff; a lines comment names rows the diff shows, changed or context, and Hive quotes them for you. Read the diff with git diff $(git merge-base HEAD <base>) in the checkout to get the line numbers right. A refused review lists every comment that needs fixing, and stores nothing. Keep comments actionable, one point each; put praise and the overview in summary. Open the diff tab with tab_open view diff when you are done.

description: Write a document. Create or replace a whole markdown (.md) or html (.html) document in Hive Drive. Folders in the path are created as needed, so file a plan as plans/auth-rewrite.md or a report as reports/2026-10/perf.md. A markdown body may open with YAML front matter between --- lines; title sets the name the user sees, and front matter that does not parse is refused rather than saved. An html document renders as a page of its own in a sandboxed frame: inline styles and scripts run; other scripts, styles and fetches load only over https; images, fonts and media load over https or as data: URLs; forms and frames do not work; a #fragment link scrolls the page and a relative link does nothing. The body is capped at 2 MiB. Answers with the entry as stored. No Drive tab opens by itself; use tab_open when the user should look now.

description: Open a tab or terminal beside the session. Ask Hive to open a tab beside this chat or Code session. view is drive (the session's documents), diff (the Code session's changes), tasks (its task board), terminal (a tmux window of the Code session) or applet:<id> (an applet whose applet.yaml lists surfaces.tab; opening it runs its page). The tab applies only while the user is viewing this chat or session, and there is no acknowledgment; a terminal's tmux window is started whether or not they are. A chat has drive and applets; diff, tasks and terminal belong to a Code session. The shared space (global) sits beside no session, so it has no tabs; the user reads it in the Drive page. path, for drive only, shows one document by its path in the space; it must exist. Omit it to leave the tab on its own pick. terminal starts a new window in the session's checkout, a shell with nothing running in it, or places one that exists. It opens detached, so it never takes the keyboard or the screen. It takes no command: run your own work yourself, and open a terminal for the user to type in. window, for terminal only, places an existing window of the session by tmux id (@3) or exact name instead of starting one, and excludes name. name, for terminal only, names the new window. The session must be running; start it in Code first. placement behind (the default) adds the tab behind the tab in front, with an unseen dot, and never takes the screen; beside splits the panel in front and opens the tab next to it, and below splits it downward, so the user sees it at once. All leave the keyboard where it is, and a tab that is already open stays where it is under any. anchor, a tab reference (drive, diff, tasks, terminal, or a window by id or name), is the tab to place relative to instead of the tab in front of the focused panel. Call it when you finish something worth looking at now, not on every write: a write while a Drive tab is open behind another tab already lights a dot on it. Use beside or below only for a result the user asked to see side by side with the terminal. If you are not sure what is open, call layout_get first.
